message.content:
**Kill VS Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate the VS Code executable (`code.exe`) with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.

```cmd
:: Kill all running instances of VS Code immediately
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – specifies the image name (process name) to target.  
* `/F` – forces termination (equivalent to “kill -9” on Unix).

If you only want to kill a specific instance, first find its PID:

```cmd
:: List all running processes named code.exe
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"

:: Suppose the PID is 1234; then kill it:
taskkill /PID 1234 /F
```

### Quick notes

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑kills **all** `code.exe` processes. |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Force‑kills a single process identified by its PID. |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | Shows all running `code.exe` processes with their PIDs. |

> **Tip:** If you’re scripting this in PowerShell, you can also do:
> ```powershell
> Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
> ```

That’s all you need to stop VS Code from the command prompt!
